measures.title: Water Quality Protection, Overdevelopment Prevention, Natural Lands Preservation, and Public Preserves General Obligation Bond Referendum
measures.summary: Asks whether Manatee County should levy an additional 0.16 mill property tax and issue up to $75,000,000 in general obligation bonds, maturing within 20 years, to acquire, improve and maintain land and property interests. The purposes are protecting drinking water sources, water quality, wildlife habitat and natural and environmentally sensitive lands from overdevelopment, and providing public preserves, with annual public audits.
measures.yesMeans: For Bonds: the County may issue up to $75 million in bonds repaid by an additional 0.16 mill property tax.
measures.noMeans: Against Bonds: the bonds and the additional 0.16 mill tax are not authorized.

measures.title: Remove Mayor's Tie Vote Right and Ex Officio President Designation; Add Mayor Not Council Member
measures.summary: Would amend the Bradenton City Charter to remove the Mayor's right to vote to break a tie and remove the Mayor's designation as ex officio president of the City Council. It would add language stating that the Mayor is not a member of the City Council.
measures.yesMeans: The Mayor no longer casts tie-breaking votes or serves as ex officio Council president, and is not a Council member.
measures.noMeans: The Mayor keeps the tie-breaking vote and the ex officio president designation.

measures.title: Providing for Term Limits for the Mayor and City Council Members
measures.summary: Would amend the Bradenton City Charter to limit the Mayor and City Council members to three full consecutive terms in the same office, beginning January 2028. After three full consecutive terms, a break in service of at least two years would be required before running again for the same office.
measures.yesMeans: The Mayor and Council members are limited to three full consecutive terms in the same office, starting January 2028.
measures.noMeans: No term limits are added for the Mayor and City Council.
